body.statement: If \(K=2\), \(q=(1,0)^{\top}\), and \(T\ge4\), then \(V_{T,2}(q;R_g,R_e)=\max\{R_e^2,a_T R_g^2/T\}\). A law \(D\in\mathfrak D_T\) is minimax if and only if \(\mathbb E_D[S_T^2]\le\max\{a_T,r_T\}\). When \(r_T\le a_T\), this is equality and the carryover-minimizing laws are exactly those supported on \(S_T\in\{-1,1\}\) for even \(T\) and on \(S_T\in\{-2,0,2\}\) for odd \(T\).
body.justification: This is the exact finite-horizon optimal design and complete optimizer face, including the parity discontinuity invisible to covariance-based design.
body.gap: Liang and Recht fix independent assignment. Thiyageswaran et al. (2026), arXiv:2601.17145v1, Appendix F.3, pp. 31--32, derive in Example 10 a Rademacher objective proportional to \((x^{\top}Lx)^2\); the immediately following paragraph relaxes \(x\) to a Gaussian vector and obtains \(\mathbb E[(x^{\top}Lx)^2]=\operatorname{Tr}(LX)^2+2\operatorname{Tr}((LX)^2)\) by Isserlis's identity. That relaxation neither characterizes realizable temporal fourth moments nor yields the exact all-law fixed-path minimax value and optimizer face.
body.consumer: A future binary N-of-1 trial with one carryover lag can select a certified assignment law and know exactly when independent toggling wastes MSE.
body.proof_tex:
Assume \(K=2\) and \(q=(1,0)^{\top}\).  By \(\texttt{def:response-matrix}\) and \(\texttt{def:error-components}\), the first column of \(A\) is \(X\), the off-diagonal entry of \(A^{\top}A\) is \(S_T\), and \(\Gamma_T^{-1}q=(1/T,0)^{\top}\).  Therefore
\[
u_T(X)=\begin{pmatrix}0\\S_T(X)/T\end{pmatrix},
\qquad v_T(X)=X/T,
\qquad F_{T,q}=I_T/T.
\]
Applying \(\texttt{lem:exact-risk-reduction}\) gives, for every \(D\in\mathfrak D_T\),
\[
\mathcal R_T(D)
=\max\!\left\{R_e^2,\frac{R_g^2}{T}\mathbb E_D[S_T^2]\right\}.
\tag{1}
\]
The pointwise certificates in \(\texttt{lem:mirrored-law-membership}\), and pairwise orthogonality \(\mathbb E_D[X_1X_T]=0\) in the odd case, imply
\[
\mathbb E_D[S_T^2]\geq a_T
\qquad\text{for every }D\in\mathfrak D_T.
\tag{2}
\]
The mirrored law belongs to \(\mathfrak D_T\) and has equality in (2).  Taking the infimum of (1) therefore proves the matching lower and upper bounds
\[
V_{T,2}(q;R_g,R_e)=\max\!\left\{R_e^2,\frac{a_TR_g^2}{T}\right\}.
\tag{3}
\]

By \(\texttt{def:lag-one-objects}\), \(r_T=TR_e^2/R_g^2\), which is well defined because both radii are positive.  Comparing (1) and (3), a feasible law is minimax exactly when
\[
\max\{r_T,\mathbb E_D[S_T^2]\}=\max\{r_T,a_T\}.
\]
Together with (2), this is equivalent to
\[
\mathbb E_D[S_T^2]\leq\max\{a_T,r_T\}.
\]
If \(r_T\leq a_T\), (2) forces equality \(\mathbb E_D[S_T^2]=a_T\).  In the even case, the nonnegative pointwise slack \(S_T^2-1\) has expectation zero exactly when \(S_T^2=1\) almost surely, or equivalently the law is supported on \(S_T\in\{-1,1\}\).  In the odd case, equality in the expected certificate requires equality in its pointwise form almost surely; the parity analysis in \(\texttt{lem:mirrored-law-membership}\) shows that this occurs exactly for \(S_T\in\{-2,0,2\}\).  Conversely any legal law with the corresponding support has second moment \(a_T\), so these conditions are also sufficient.  This proves the complete optimizer face and its primal and parity-dual certificates.
